_note: Every sound in the game (§6 of MILESTONES: sixteen sounds, three music layers). Sound EFFECTS are synthesised in the browser from the specs below; MUSIC is generated offline by Lyria and shipped as files. See _whyNote.
_whyNote: Gemini has Lyria 3 for music and TTS for speech, and NO dedicated sound-effects model — checked against the API docs, not assumed. Prompting a music model for a 90ms shotgun report gets you a short piece of music about a shotgun. So effects are synthesised: oscillators, noise and envelopes through Web Audio. That is also the better answer for this game. It matches the architecture already here (a hand-written PNG codec rather than sharp, an atlas built from a manifest), it adds no dependency and no download, every sound is a few numbers you can tune in this file, and retro synthesis is stylistically right for pixel art in a way a recorded sample is not.
_specNote: wave: sine|square|saw|triangle|noise. freq/freqTo sweep over the sound's life. decay is seconds. Sounds are polyphonic and rate-limited per key so sixty hits in a frame do not stack into a wall — see limitPerSecond.

master._muteNote: Both persist to localStorage under rdf.audio so a muted player stays muted.
master._sampleGainNote: Generated samples arrive normalised to roughly full scale, while the synth path peaks far lower for the same `gain` value — measured 1.0 against about 0.12. Reusing one gain for both would make every sampled effect about twice as loud as its synthesised neighbour and clip when several overlap. Sample playback is scaled by this instead of retuning sixteen hand-set gains.

shootLight._note: Scattergun, Sidearm, Nail Gun. Short and dry; it fires constantly, so anything with a tail becomes a drone.
shootLight.prompt: A short, dry shotgun report. Close-miked, punchy, no reverb tail, no music. Single shot.

shootHeavy._note: Varmint Rifle, Grenade Launcher, Drum Gun.
shootHeavy.prompt: A heavy hunting rifle firing once. Deep crack with a short low thump, dry, no echo, no music.

swing._note: Pitchfork and Sledge. A whoosh, not an impact — the impact is a separate sound and they must not merge.
swing.prompt: A heavy iron tool swung fast through air. Low whoosh, no impact, no music.

crit._note: Deliberately brighter and a fifth up from `hit`, so a crit is audible in a crowd without being louder.

enemyDeath.prompt: A wet, muffled thud of a body dropping onto dry soil. Short, dull, no music.

playerHurt._note: Never rate-limited below the i-frame cadence: missing the sound that tells you you are dying is the one unacceptable drop.
playerHurt.prompt: A blunt heavy impact on a person, muffled and painful. Short, dry, no voice, no music.

mine._note: The pickaxe tick. Quiet and frequent — it is a texture that tells you the tool is working, not an event.
mine.prompt: A single pickaxe strike chipping stone. Sharp click with a little grit, very short, no echo, no music.

nodeBreak.prompt: A rock splitting and crumbling into rubble. Sharp crack then falling debris, dry, no music.

explosion.prompt: A compact explosion in an open field. Sharp blast with a short low rumble, no long tail, no music.

bossTell._note: The Bull pawing the ground. Low, rising, and long enough to react to — §9 wants every attack telegraphed.
bossTell.prompt: A huge animal snorting and scraping a heavy hoof through dry dirt. Menacing, low, no music.

shootLauncher.prompt: A loud grenade launcher firing. Deep hollow THUMP with a metallic clank, punchy and immediate, close-miked. Single shot, dry, no reverb.
shootLauncher._gainNote: Generated quiet (peak 0.05 against most effects' 0.9). Compensated here rather than spending another generation on it — gain is free, credits are not.

shootBurst._note: Drum Gun. Heard in bursts, so it must stay tight.
shootBurst.prompt: A single round from a light machine gun. Sharp mechanical crack, dry, close, no echo, no music.

shootNail.prompt: A thick glob of tar launched from a tube. Wet compressed pop then a short airy whoosh, no music.

shootHarpoon.prompt: A harpoon gun firing. Sharp metallic snap then a rope hissing out fast, dry, no music.

spray._note: Chem Sprayer. Loops while held, so it must not have a hard attack.
spray.prompt: A pressurised chemical sprayer hissing. Steady wet aerosol hiss, no start or stop, no music.

sledgeHit._note: Sledge landing. The impact, not the swing.
sledgeHit.prompt: A sledgehammer slamming into packed earth. Deep heavy thud with a little debris, dry, no music.

scytheSpin.prompt: A curved blade sweeping through air in an arc. Smooth low whoosh, no impact, no music.

dogBark.prompt: A single sharp farm dog bark. Close, dry, no echo, no music, no other animals.

baitDrop.prompt: A heavy grain sack dropping onto dirt. Dull soft thud with a grain shift, no music.

igniteFire._note: Fire element, and a slick catching.
igniteFire.prompt: Fire catching and flaring up across spilled fuel. Whoosh then crackling flame, no music.

acidSizzle.prompt: Corrosive acid hissing and eating into metal. Wet aggressive sizzle, no music.

freezeHit.prompt: Ice crystallising fast over a surface. Sharp brittle crackle with a glassy ring, no music.

chop.prompt: An axe biting into a tree trunk. Sharp woody thock, dry, no echo, no music.

treeFall.prompt: A tree cracking and falling to the ground. Splintering wood then a heavy leafy crash, no music.

dash.prompt: A fast whoosh of someone sprinting past, with a scuff of dirt. Short, dry, no music.

digIn.prompt: Boots planting hard into soil and bracing. Gritty crunch then a low settle, no music.

lowHealth._note: Pulses under about a quarter health. Deliberately unpleasant.

gameOver._note: Falls rather than rises. The only sound in the game that does.

bossDeath._note: The Duster does not explode (§9) — it coughs and stops.
bossDeath.prompt: A large diesel engine coughing, sputtering and dying. Mechanical failure winding down to silence, no music.

music._note: Three layers (§6). Generated offline by `npm run music` with Lyria 3 and committed to public/audio as mp3 — a music model is the right tool for music, and generating it at runtime would be a network call in a game loop. Layers cross-fade rather than cut.
music._promptNote: These prompts are the source of truth for the soundtrack. Re-running the tool regenerates from them; tune the prose, not the audio.

field._when: Waves 1-11. The farm is still a farm.
field.prompt: Sparse, unhurried instrumental Americana. Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and a lonely pedal steel over a slow brushed snare. Warm, rural, slightly melancholy, like an empty field at dusk. No vocals. Loopable, steady tempo around 84 BPM, no dramatic build.

combat._when: Waves 12-24, and any wave with heavy pressure.
combat.prompt: Driving instrumental country-rock with menace. Palm-muted electric guitar riff, insistent kick and tambourine, low fiddle drone underneath. Rural horror, not action-movie heroics. No vocals. Loopable, around 128 BPM, relentless rather than building.

boss.prompt: Heavy, slow, dread-filled instrumental. Detuned baritone guitar, groaning cello, sparse thunderous drum hits with lots of space between them. The sound of something very large and very patient. No vocals. Loopable, around 70 BPM, oppressive.

_sourceNote: Each effect declares its source. ElevenLabs has a purpose-built text-to-sound-effects API and Gemini does not, so PHYSICAL sounds — gunfire, impacts, stone, a bull scraping dirt — are generated there, where a real generator beats an oscillator outright. ARCADE feedback stays synthesised on purpose: an XP pickup, a level-up flourish and a UI blip are not real-world sounds, and a realistic recording of one would fight the pixel art rather than serve it. Vampire Survivors and Brotato both use synthetic blips for exactly this reason.
_fallbackNote: EVERY sound keeps its synth spec, including the ElevenLabs ones. The engine prefers a loaded sample and falls back to synthesis when the file is absent, so the game is fully audible with no API key at all and degrades one sound at a time rather than going silent.
_durationNote: ElevenLabs enforces a 0.5s minimum, and several of these want to be 70ms. The generated file therefore carries trailing silence; that is harmless because playback is one-shot and the decay is in the audio.
_countNote: Thirty-eight effects. The milestone asks for sixteen; sixteen covers a game where every gun sounds the same. Each weapon has its own voice, each element announces itself, and the two abilities and both boss deaths are distinct, because a player who cannot hear which of six weapons just fired cannot tell what their build is doing.
_promptLessonNote: shootLauncher first came back near-silent from a prompt built mostly of negatives (no explosion, no music). Describing what the sound IS, loudly and concretely, gets a usable file; listing what it is not gets an empty one. Worth checking new generations for silence — the tool cannot, since a valid MP3 of nothing is still a valid MP3.
